## What is Lattice?


Lattice is a[performance management](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/performance-management-systems/) and talent management platform that helps HR teams run performance reviews, set and track goals and OKRs, manage 1:1s, gather continuous feedback, run engagement surveys, and handle compensation planning, all inside a single system called the Lattice Talent Suite.


Despite its popularity, Lattice has drawn recurring criticism over pricing, administrative complexity, and product limitations that emerge as teams scale. The most consistent feedback across sources including G2 centers on administrative friction, cascading OKR setups that grow convoluted at scale, reporting rigid enough to force spreadsheet workarounds, and calendar sync issues in the 1:1 module.


## Why teams look for Lattice alternatives in 2026?


Lattice offers comprehensive features across performance and engagement, yet HR leaders often look for alternatives as their teams grow and priorities shift.


#### Pricing stacks fast


Starts at $13/seat, but add-ons push the full stack to $27/seat/month.


#### Complex OKR setup


Cascading goals across levels requires manual clicks at every hierarchy layer.


#### Rigid reporting


Reports break under multi-dimensional filtering, forcing spreadsheet exports.


#### Limited bulk uploads


Templates, question banks, and review data often need one-by-one setup.


#### Buried admin features


Key features sit deep in the admin console, with weak UX for daily admins.

## Detailed breakdown: 8 Lattice alternatives worth evaluating


### 1. Culture Amp


Best for teams looking for in-depth benchmarking


Pricing: Contact sales


★ G2: 4.5/5


Culture Amp is an employee experience solution built around engagement, performance, and development. The platform leans into[engagement analytics](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/people-analytics-strategy/) , with benchmark comparisons available alongside standard reporting.


#### Key features


- Pulse and lifecycle surveys with peer benchmarking across industry segments
- Performance reviews with[calibration grids](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/the-9-box-grid-talent-management/) and[360-degree feedback workflows](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/360-degree-feedback-examples/)
- Retention insights and DEI diagnostics from aggregated engagement data
- AI Coach for skill development suggestions and automated feedback analysis


#### Cons


- Performance reviews can feel clunky compared to the engagement tools.
- Review cycles offer limited custom reminders and notifications.
- Survey question setup is limited and doesn’t support multi-faceted questions.


### 2. Peoplebox


Best for HR leaders tying goals to performance with automated workflows


Pricing: $8/user/mo


★ G2: 4.5/5


Peoplebox is an AI-first talent management solution built around OKRs, performance reviews, engagement, and 360 feedback. The platform natively syncs OKR progress from Jira and other work tools, and includes AI-driven goal creation and review summaries.


#### Key features


- OKR management with automated sync from Jira, HubSpot, and other work tools
- Performance reviews with[360 feedback](https://www.peoplebox.ai/360-degree-employee-reviews-software/) , calibration, and self-review workflows
- Engagement pulse surveys with sentiment analysis and action tracking dashboards
- AI-powered goal creation, review summaries, and continuous feedback nudges


#### Limitations


- Custom reporting could be more flexible for deeper analytics views
- Automation features could expand for repetitive HR workflows
- New buyers benefit from guided onboarding to unlock full breadth

Compare Peoplebox vs Lattice across your people management workflows, from performance reviews to engagement.

### 3. Leapsome


Best for teams that need performance & learning under one roof


Pricing: Contact sales


★ G2: 4.8/5


Leapsome is a people-enablement suite that combines performance, engagement, learning, and compensation with a native HRIS layer. The platform operates in 38 languages and serves mid-market to enterprise organizations.


#### Key features


- [Performance reviews with 360-degree feedback](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/360-degree-review-template-blog/)
- Native learning management with course library
- Cascading OKRs from company to individual level
- HRIS layer with employee records and onboarding


#### Limitations


- Backend setup can feel complex for HR admins during onboarding
- Notification overload can happen when review cycles overlap
- OKR updates often need manual data entry with limited automation


### 4. 15Five


Best for AI-assisted manager coaching


Pricing: $16/person/mo


★ G2: 4.6/5


15Five is a performance management platform built around weekly check-ins, 1:1s, OKRs, and engagement pulses. The platform positions manager coaching as the core lever, with the Kona AI coach guiding conversations in real time.


#### Key features


- Weekly employee-manager check-ins on priorities and blockers
- AI-powered manager coaching through Kona
- [Peer recognition](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/peer-review-examples/) through built-in High Fives
- Performance reviews with 360-degree feedback


#### Limitations


- Survey and review design can feel rigid with limited customization
- Reporting dashboards can be hard to customize for deeper analytics
- Some advanced features sit behind higher-tier pricing plans


### 5. Betterworks


Best for multi-region enterprise HR operations


Pricing: $9/person/mo


★ G2: 4.4/5


Betterworks is an enterprise performance management platform focused on OKRs, continuous calibration, and multi-region deployment. The platform includes private-hosted AI infrastructure that keeps performance data inside the customer environment.


#### Key features


- Cascading OKRs from company level down to individual
- [Continuous calibration](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/quarterly-business-review-template-for-hr/) that runs outside review cycles
- AI-powered goal drafting and review summaries
- Multi-region deployment with 20+ language support


#### Limitations


- Customization for goal creation and workflows could be more flexible
- Integrations with Jira, Outlook, and Teams could be tighter
- Text formatting in reports is limited, with no bold or italic options


### 6. PerformYard


Best for teams with highly tailored review processes


Pricing: $5/person/mo


★ G2: 4.7/5


PerformYard is a focused performance management platform built around highly configurable review cycles. The platform is designed for organizations that need to adapt review formats to their specific processes rather than fit into a rigid template.


#### Key features


- Performance reviews with 360-degree feedback
- Continuous feedback between peers and managers
- [Historical performance trends](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/top-performance-appraisal-software/) per employee across years
- Support team builds custom review forms for your workflow


#### Limitations


- Dashboards are static with no Gantt or timeline views
- Multi-step workflows require many clicks to complete
- Notification volume can overwhelm employees during active cycles


### 7. Engagedly


Best for mid-market HR tying performance to rewards


Pricing: $8/person/mo


★ G2: 4.3/5


Engagedly is an all-in-one[talent management platform](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/9-box-talent-review/) combining performance, goals, engagement, learning, and rewards. The platform is positioned for SMB and mid-market teams that want multiple talent modules in one system.


#### Key features


- Performance reviews with 360-degree feedback
- Goals and OKRs with cascading and progress tracking
- Built-in learning management system with course library
- Rewards and recognition with peer-to-peer shoutouts


#### Limitations


- Marissa AI and AI summaries feel underdeveloped in current form
- Platform loading speed can be slow, especially on mobile
- HRIS syncing has recurring integration issues
- Goals module has too many screens and unclear navigation


### 8. Workleap (Officevibe)


Best for lightweight engagement listening for SMBs


Pricing: $4,999/year


★ G2: 4.3/5


Workleap (formerly Officevibe) is an employee experience platform built around anonymous pulse surveys and manager coaching. The platform is positioned for SMB and lower mid-market teams that lead with engagement measurement over formal performance management.


#### Key features


- Anonymous pulse surveys with automated cadences
- Performance reviews with continuous check-ins
- Manager-focused action plans from anonymous team feedback
- eNPS tracking with historical trend views


#### Limitations


- Pulse survey questions cannot be edited from pre-set templates
- Support tickets can take up to 3 days for urgent issues
- Limited export options for sharing insights outside the platform


## How we evaluated the 8 Lattice alternatives


Every platform in this guide was assessed under the same criteria, using verified data and consistent thresholds, so the shortlist reflects real buyer fit rather than opinion or paid placement.


### Data sources


- **G2 verified reviews:** 5,000+ verified reviews across all 8 platforms, analysed for recurring themes.
- **Vendor product documentation:** Feature claims from vendor product pages, cross-checked against G2 reviewer confirmations.
- **Published pricing pages:** Verified on September 2026, with custom-quote products labeled.
- **[Peoplebox research team](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/hr-metrics/) :** Independent review of pages, features, and content depth across all 8 alternatives.


### Selection framework


1. **Product-category overlap:** Must cover performance management, goals/OKRs, or engagement at feature parity with Lattice’s Talent Suite
2. **Independent analyst coverage:** Reviewed on G2, Capterra, and Gartner Peer Insights across multiple review platforms
3. **Segment coverage:** Represents SMB, mid-market, or enterprise buyer profiles across the final list
4. **Distinct positioning:** Offers a wedge no other shortlisted product covers
5. **2026 relevance:** Actively developing product with a public roadmap and current customer base


## What actually matters when picking a Lattice alternative


The eight platforms above cover the credible switching paths from Lattice in 2026, each built around a distinct primary strength across engagement, OKRs, learning, and performance. The market has fragmented enough that no single platform wins on every dimension.


What determines success after switching is not the platform itself but how tightly its strongest capability matches the team’s most-cited pain point with Lattice. The best replacement is not the closest match to Lattice; it is the closest match to why you left it.

## FAQ


1. What are the best Lattice alternatives in 2026? The top Lattice alternatives in 2026 are Culture Amp for[engagement benchmarking](https://www.peoplebox.ai/best-employee-engagement-software/) , Peoplebox for[OKR automation](https://www.peoplebox.ai/okr-software/) , Leapsome for[performance and learning](https://www.peoplebox.ai/performance-reviews-software/) , 15Five for[manager coaching](https://www.peoplebox.ai/one-on-one-meeting-software/) , Betterworks for[enterprise HR operations](https://www.peoplebox.ai/performance-management-software/) , PerformYard for[tailored reviews](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/performance-review-form/) , Engagedly for rewards-linked performance, and Workleap for lightweight SMB[engagement listening](https://www.peoplebox.ai/employee-pulse-surveys/) .


2. What are the main reasons HR leaders look for Lattice alternative? The main reasons to leave Lattice are pricing that stacks quickly (Foundations at $13 per seat plus add-ons pushes the full stack to $27),[cascading OKR setups](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/google-okr-playbook/) that require manual clicks at every hierarchy layer,[rigid reporting](https://www.peoplebox.ai/blog/hr-dashboard/) that forces spreadsheet exports, and admin features buried in the console.


3. How does Lattice pricing compare to competitors? Lattice starts at $13 per seat per month, with add-ons pushing the full stack to around $27. In a Lattice competitors pricing comparison, PerformYard begins at $5, Peoplebox at $8, Betterworks at $9, and 15Five at $16. Leapsome, Culture Amp, and Workleap use custom pricing.


4. Which Lattice alternatives work best for mid-market HR teams? For mid-market HR teams (100 to 1,000 employees), the strongest Lattice alternatives are[Peoplebox](https://www.peoplebox.ai/) for OKR automation across the HR tech stack, Leapsome for combining performance with native learning modules, Culture Amp for[engagement benchmarking at scale](https://www.peoplebox.ai/engagement-insights/) , and 15Five for manager coaching rituals with[weekly check-ins](https://www.peoplebox.ai/weekly-check-ins/) .


5. Which Lattice alternatives support continuous performance management for remote teams? For continuous performance management with remote teams, 15Five leads with weekly check-ins and Kona AI coach for manager 1:1s. Peoplebox syncs OKR progress from Jira and other work tools. Leapsome offers instant feedback and cascading OKRs. Manager adoption determines success more than any single feature.


6. Do Lattice alternatives integrate with Slack and Microsoft Teams? Yes, most Lattice alternatives offer Slack integration and Microsoft Teams integration as part of the standard HR tech stack. Peoplebox, Leapsome, 15Five, Culture Amp, and Betterworks all support both. Depth varies: some run full workflows inside Slack or Teams, others send notifications only. Manager adoption depends on depth.
